newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX ends bourse trade weaker, Dow weighs.
newsitem.headline: German DAX ends bourse trade weaker, Dow weighs.

text.p: German blue-chip shares closed bourse dealings lower Thursday, as the market was pulled down by overnight losses on Wall Street and a weaker Bund, which slipped after the Bundesbank left interest rates unchanged.
The 30-share DAX index closed down 22.24 points at 2,680.75, while the IBIS DAX, which records day-long computer dealings, was off 6.12 points at 2,679.11.
"We're seeing a bit of caution with Wall Street down," said one trader.
Most of the market interest focused on telecommunications and chemical sector shares.
Utilities firms Veba and RWE continued to rally after RWE said it would join Veba's alliance with British-based Cable & Wireless to create a challenger to monopoly Deutsche Telekom.
Veba ended bourse trade up 86 pfennigs to rise to 82.39 marks, while RWE was up 87 pfennigs at 61.47 marks.

Utility firm Viag continued to slide after RWE said on Wednesday it would pull out of talks on a partnership with the Bavarian company and British Telecom and was not bucked even after it said the deal with BT would go ahead.
Viag ended floor dealings down 6.80 marks at 574.20.
The chemicals and car sectors did worse than average and traders said both were affected by profit-taking.
One exception was sports carmaker Porsche which hit a bourse year high of 1,090 marks and closed up eight marks at 1,083, following a positive profits report.
Carmaker Volkswagen, on the other hand, lost nine marks to end floor trade at 572.25 marks, after it said it was recalling 21,600 cars made at a plant in Portugal.
Chemical companies Bayer, Hoechst and BASF all lost ground even though Hoechst and BASF both announced new joint-ventures earlier in the day.

Bayer fell 62 pfennigs to 57.47 marks in bourse trade, BASF closed down 1.20 at 48.75 marks and Hoechst was off 92 pfennigs at 57.60 marks. "The sector is due for a bit of a sell off," said one dealer.
